title.narrative: Strengthening Public Finance Management Systems and Reforms and Combating Corruption

description.narrative: Bangladesh has made significant socio-economic progress, attaining lower-middle-income status in 2015. Since 2000, GDP growth has averaged nearly 6% annually. The country aims to reach upper-middle-income status by 2031, with the Eighth Five-Year Plan (2021-2025) prioritizing Public Finance Management (PFM) reforms through the PFM Action Plan (2024-2028). Over the past three decades, Bangladesh has strengthened its PFM systems as a key governance pillar. To address remaining challenges, the PFM Action Plans (2018-2023 and 2024-2028) support the implementation of the broader PFM Reform Strategy (2016-2021). Based on the 2021 Public Expenditure and Financial Accountability (PEFA) assessment, a new PFM Reform Strategy (2025-2030) is being developed to transition to a technology-driven, efficient public expenditure management system.Weak PFM systems and high corruption levels have historically hindered efficient, transparent service delivery. Corruption remains a major development challenge, impacting state revenue and long-term economic growth.The Interim Government, led by Nobel laureate Dr. Muhammad Yunus following the July/August 2024 popular uprising, is implementing wide-ranging reforms. PFM and anti-corruption efforts are central to this agenda. With the new government in place, the EU has a strategic opportunity to deepen its engagement. In September 2024, Dr. Yunus met Commission President Ursula Von der Leyen at the UN General Assembly, requesting EU support for ongoing reforms, particularly anti-corruption. President Von der Leyen reaffirmed the EU¿s commitment.Since 2008, the EU has been a key partner in PFM reforms through the Trust Fund programme, which has driven regulatory improvements, digitalization of transactions via iBAS++, a new classification system, and enhanced expenditure management through the Medium-Term Budgeting Framework (MTBF). The Strengthening Public Expenditure Management Program - Bank Executed Trust Fund (SPEMP-BETF) has been instrumental in implementing the PFM Action Plan, despite recent disruptions. Key achievements include the finalization of the Medium & Long-Term Revenue Strategy (MLTRS) for the National Board of Revenue (NBR) and the development of the PFM Reform Strategy (2025-2030).Through bilateral PFM Technical Assistance (TA), the EU has supported the National Board of Revenue (NBR), the Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General (OCAG), and the National Parliament¿s Financial Oversight Committees (FoCs). Achievements include the digitalization of tax return filing, progress in transfer pricing, professional training programs, and the establishment of a budget helpdesk for MPs. However, both ongoing PFM programs will conclude in June 2025. To ensure the efficient use of public resources and improved public service delivery, the EU remains committed to supporting sustainable, digitalized PFM systems and institutions, leveraging digital solutions to combat corruption and enhance institutional capacity.The proposed Action aims to contribute to the Multi-annual Indicative Programme (MIP) 2021-2027 Priority Area 3 ¿ Inclusive Governance, specifically addressing the following Specific Objective: SO 3: Public service delivery and financial/fiscal management are improved through digital governance. Together with other development partners like World Bank (WB), Asian Development Bank (ADB), International Monitory Fund (IMF), Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), this Action will support the government to implement the PFM Reform Strategy
